peerMapping.justification: The block is built around COPPER as a pro-cyclical industrial metal with 6.262 USD millions displayed 24-hour perp liquidity. The peer set is not a generic commodity basket: SILVER and GOLD express the shared US dollar and real-rate channel, CL and NATGAS express global growth plus energy input costs into mining and smelting, and TSLA, NVDA, and BE express electrification, data-center power, and distributed-energy demand for copper. Weights are positive binary fractions that sum to exactly 1, with the largest weight on the most comparable liquid metal and smaller weights where the economic link is indirect or displayed liquidity in USD millions is low.

peers.name: Silver
peers.reason: Closest cross-commodity peer: silver shares the US dollar and real-rate channel with copper, has meaningful industrial demand, and is often co-produced with copper, while its 32.581 USD millions liquidity supports the largest weight.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Tesla ties copper to electric vehicles, charging, and storage, where copper intensity per vehicle is high; the single-name equity risk and 4.787 USD millions liquidity argue for a moderate weight.

peers.name: WTI crude oil
peers.reason: WTI crude oil shares copper's global growth, industrial activity, and reflation channel, and energy also feeds mining and smelting costs. CL has very deep displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 40.091 USD millions, but oil has separate supply shocks, so it ranks below silver.

peers.name: Gold
peers.reason: Common macro factor is the US dollar and real yields; it adds the risk-off side of the metal complex while copper is the more industrial side. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 23.982 USD millions, so it receives a high but smaller weight than SILVER.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is included for data-center and AI capex that pulls power-grid, cooling, and electrification demand, plus a broad risk-on channel, rather than as a generic tech holding. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 4.508 USD millions, close to TSLA, so it receives a similar small weight.

peers.name: Natural gas
peers.reason: Natural gas captures the input-cost channel through power and fuel used in refining and smelting, but the link is narrower than the metal-complex and global-growth peers. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is only 2.186 USD millions, so the weight is kept small.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: Copper's dominant risk is cyclical global-growth and risk-on or risk-off shocks. The S&P 500 is the deepest listed risk-asset proxy in CORE_UNIVERSE, with displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 50.729 USD millions, making it the most practical single instrument to position opposite copper and offset that growth beta.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract
